big: Rohan and Meena invest ₹10,000 a month for 20 years into the same fund, assuming the same 12% before costs. They only differ in one thing: the plan they chose.

lines: The Regular plan costs only 0.8% more per year. Surely that is nothing?
Let us find out. Watch what 0.8% a year does to a growing balance over twenty years.

alt: Two sets of bars comparing the final amount in a Direct plan and a Regular plan
caps: Same fund, same 12% before costs, ₹10,000 every month.
After 10 years the Direct plan is already ahead.
After 20 years the gap is about ₹9.03 lakh.
An assumed rate, not a promise. The point is that costs compound too.

intro: Beyond the yearly charge, two choices matter.
rows: A fee if you sell within a set period, often a year
Profits stay in and keep compounding, with no payouts
Money is paid out to you from time to time, and the unit price drops by that amount
note: Read the exit load before you buy, not when you sell.

q: Why does a 1% yearly cost reduce the final sum by so much over twenty years?
opts: Because the fee is charged only in the last year, when the balance is largest
Because the fee increases by 1% each year until the fund is closed
It is charged on a growing balance each year, and lost money stops compounding
Because the fee is paid by you separately and never shows in the fund's value
why: The charge is taken every year, not at the end. Spread over twenty years it adds up steadily.
The expense ratio is a yearly rate, not a rising one. It does not climb by itself each year.
Each year's fee takes a slice of a larger balance, and that slice would have kept growing.
The fee is taken inside the fund, so it lowers the unit price without any separate bill.

q: Rohan buys the Direct plan and Meena the Regular plan of the same fund. What is true about their portfolios?
opts: The two plans hold the same companies. Only the yearly charge differs
Rohan's fund holds better companies because Direct plans have a stronger manager
Meena's fund holds safer bonds since a distributor guides her choices
Rohan cannot invest through an SIP because Direct plans need lump sums
why: Same portfolio, same manager. A Regular plan's higher charge pays the distributor's service.
Both plans share the same manager and holdings. The difference is in how the fund is bought and paid for.
A Regular plan does not hold different bonds. The distributor sells it but does not change the holdings.
Direct plans accept SIPs as well as lump sums, through the fund house or platforms.

q: A Regular plan costs more. When might it still be worth it?
opts: Never, since Direct plans always give better results to every investor
Only when the fund is brand new and has no track record to judge
When you want a higher return, since Regular plans promise more growth
When adviser help keeps you on plan and you accept paying for it
why: Direct is cheaper, but not always the better outcome if a person would not manage it well alone.
A fund's age has no link to which plan makes sense, so this is not a real reason.
Regular plans do not promise higher returns. Their extra cost lowers returns, not raises them.
Paying for good guidance can be worthwhile if it stops costly mistakes. Know what you are paying.

q: Meena sells her units after 9 months and is charged 1% on the amount. What caused this?
opts: The expense ratio, charged on every sale of units
An exit load, charged because she sold within the set period
Tax, charged on all sales whatever the holding time
A penalty for investing through an SIP instead of a lump sum
why: The expense ratio is a yearly charge inside the fund, not a fee on a sale.
An exit load applies when you sell before the set period ends, often a year, to discourage quick selling.
Tax is a separate matter and depends on gains and the holding period, not a flat 1%.
How you bought has no bearing on this. The charge comes from selling too early.

pts: The expense ratio is taken inside the fund every year, so you never see a bill.
A Direct plan costs less than a Regular plan of the same fund. Same portfolio, smaller charge.
Check the exit load before you buy, and pick Growth or IDCW on purpose.
